newsitem.title: DUBAI: Air cargo industry needs improved cooperation.
newsitem.headline: Air cargo industry needs improved cooperation.

text.p: Serious efforts must be made towards improving dialogue between shippers, airlines, freight forwarders and integrated operators in order to find solutions to the air industry's problems, the European Air Shippers Council(EASC) secretary-general, Chris Welsh said.

In a comment on the differing relationships between shippers -- exporters and distributors --, airlines and freight forwarders, Welsh said there was a need "to get rid of this ridiculous nervousness of airlines not being able to talk directly to shippers...no other industry would understand this situation."

He told the 18th Air Cargo Forum(ACF) meeting here on Wednesday: "There needs to be a firm commitment by both carriers and shippers to each other and to the various other partners involved in the air cargo supply chain...we need firm commitment from the players concerned to improve service standards and provide innovative service standards.

"Above all we need an air cargo industry that works...it must understand that the pressures of technological change in manufacturing processes, the greater demands made on shippers for improved quality by their customers mean the pressure is on shippers to compress the supply chain and reduce (customers') costs," he added.

"When information can now flow in seconds, distribution, transport, warehousing, lorries and planes are increasinlgy seen by industry as constraints or limiting factors in the supply chain cycle times," Welsh said.

"Automated ordering and the use of electronic data interchange in paying for goods are becoming more commonplace. In some sectors, the prospects of teleshopping, home deliveries and more customised or differentiated products are just around the corner. How will the airline industry meet these needs?"

He also warned about the impact of environmental pressures and saidthe adoption of industry "best practice" standards was likely to be key factor in avoiding punitive taxes or charges for inefficient or environmentally unfriendly methods of transport.
Welsh said the EASC plans to convene a European Cargo Industry Forum to act as a catalyst for improved industry relations.
